audit.whatIsWrong: Five fields described Winds of War as a 'shield-and-slow zoning' tool (spikes[0].text, early, whys[0], wants.you[0], wants.foe[0]). Winds of War has no shield and no slow. Justice Punch was called a knockback throughout, and Shield of Durand's taunt — the single most dangerous thing in the matchup for a soldier-dependent champion — was never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Riot's text: Winds of War is two windblasts converging into a tornado that deals damage over time (825 range, 11/10/9/8/7). The shield and slow belong to Shield of Durand (275 range, 18s at rank 1), which ends in a taunt. Justice Punch knocks UP the first enemy champion it encounters from 650 — 'first champion' is the actionable half and it was missing. Colossal Smash is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the tell.
audit.corrected: Each ability given its own effect: tornado damage-over-time, taunt inside 275, knockup on the first champion at 650, and a 180-second Hero's Entrance.
sources: brief enemyKit P/Q/W/E/R text and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer said Skill for rows 2 through 6; content and the packet both said Galio for levels 3, 4-5 and 6 and Azir for the two item rows.
audit.why: He holds two engages from level 3 and a 4000-range ult at 6; the lane turns when Nashor's shred arrives and his 180-second ult spends most of the game on cooldown. Azir's 45.41% win rate is consistent with losing the lane and winning the scaling.
audit.corrected: Rows 2-4 to Galio, rows 5-6 to Azir, every why rewritten to argue the row it sits under.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] credited his global ult at level 3; mid claimed Hero's Entrance lets him 'reset back' after roaming; whys[4], mid and spikes[2] all spiked on 'Conquer the Sands'.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance exists at 6, is 180 seconds at rank 1 and is a one-way trip — Riot's text has him designate an ally's position and smash down there. Azir's Q is Conquering Sands; 'Conquer the Sands' and 'Conquer wave clear' are fabricated names.
audit.corrected: Ult timing and cooldown stated correctly, the one-way nature used as the reason his roam costs him the wave, and the Azir ability named properly.
sources: brief enemyKit R text and cd

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit; dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7 — the window is seven to eleven seconds. Shield of Durand 18s, Hero's Entrance 180s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Real numbers in both fields plus the ult timer, which is the one worth tracking on a clock.

notes: The central defect was a misattributed kit: five fields gave Winds of War a shield and a slow it does not have. Riot's text makes it a damage-over-time tornado; the shield and slow are Shield of Durand, whose release TAUNTS inside 275 — and the taunt appeared nowhere on the page despite being the interaction that most punishes a champion who fights through soldiers. Justice Punch was also called a knockback everywhere; it is a knockup, and it only affects the FIRST champion it encounters, which is why keeping a body on his charge line matters. Hero's Entrance was described as letting him 'reset back' after roaming — it is a one-way 4000-range arrival on a 180-second cooldown at rank 1, which is why his roam costs him the wave. 'Conquer the Sands' / 'Conquer wave clear' was a fabricated name for Conquering Sands in three fields. Chart: full said Skill for rows 2-6 while content and the packet said Galio x3 then Azir x2; aligned with rewritten whys. phases[N].rating untouched — see questions. Not asserted: what the taunt does to Azir's soldier autos or whether soldiers keep attacking while he is taunted, and whether Emperor's Divide's terrain stops the Justice Punch charge. Neither is answerable from Riot's text.
